sections.heading: PiyApi | LongMemEval Benchmark Results
paragraphs: Long-term memory remains one of the least solved and least rigorously evaluated capabilities in production AI systems.

We present PiyApi , Negentro's first-generation long-term memory engine, and evaluate it against LongMemEval, the most comprehensive benchmark for conversational memory retrieval. PiyApi achieves state-of-the-art results across all recall depths, reaching [YOUR_OVERALL_SCORE]% overall accuracy using [YOUR_MODEL] as the answering model.

Notably, these results were obtained without any question-specific prompt engineering, and without large frontier models, absorbing errors within the benchmark itself, which represent a ceiling on possible score improvement. pages.raw_text: Abstract Long-term memory remains one of the least solved and least rigorously evaluated capabilities in production AI systems. We present PiyApi , Negentro's first-generation long-term memory engine, and evaluate it against LongMemEval, the most comprehensive benchmark for conversational memory retrieval. PiyApi achieves state-of-the-art results across all recall depths, reaching [YOUR_OVERALL_SCORE]% overall accuracy using [YOUR_MODEL] as the answering model. Notably, these results were obtained without any question-specific prompt engineering, and without large frontier models, absorbing errors within the benchmark itself, which represent a ceiling on possible score improvement. We report our methodology, results, and analysis, including a discussion of evaluation ceiling effects encountered at high accuracy levels.

pages.title: 1. Context & Benchmark

sections.heading: 1.1 Why We Chose LongMemEval
paragraphs: While early benchmarks focused on simple factual recall over limited context windows, building production AI requires evaluating how memory systems handle the messy reality of long-term human-AI interactions. Facts evolve, users contradict themselves, and crucial details are scattered across dozens of disjointed sessions.

We chose LONGMEMEVAL (Wu et al.) because it establishes a rigorous, scientifically backed standard for this exact complexity. It introduces a highly sophisticated evaluation model that mathematically formulates memory interactions as a 4-tuple sequence:

Under this paradigm, the system must process an extensive, continuously growing sequence of sessions \( \mathcal{S} \), where each session \( S_i \) has a specific timestamp \( t_i \). To succeed, an engine must correctly synthesize an answer \( a \) to a user query \( q \) asked at time \( t_q \) (where \( t_q > t_N \)).

This dynamic formulation perfectly tests the core pillars of conversational AI. By reflecting real-world chronological interactions rather than static documents, LongMemEval stands as the premier benchmark for measuring true conversational persistence.

sections.heading: 1.2 What is LongMemEval?
paragraphs: LongMemEval uses a rigorous dataset of 500 questions embedded within freely scalable user-assistant chat histories. We evaluated using the longmemeval_s setting, which contains approximately 115k tokens per problem (57M tokens total).
The dataset challenges the memory layer across five distinct core abilities:

definition_lists.definition: Ability to recall specific information from extensive interactive histories, including details mentioned by either the user or the assistant.
Ability to synthesize information across multiple history sessions to answer complex questions that involve aggregation and comparison.
Ability to recognize changes in the user's personal information and update the knowledge dynamically over time.
Awareness of temporal aspects of user information, including both explicit time mentions and timestamp metadata in interactions.
Ability to identify questions seeking unknown information (not mentioned in the history) and answer correctly by abstaining.

Context & Benchmark 1.1 Why We Chose LongMemEval While early benchmarks focused on simple factual recall over limited context windows, building production AI requires evaluating how memory systems handle the messy reality of long-term human-AI interactions. Facts evolve, users contradict themselves, and crucial details are scattered across dozens of disjointed sessions. We chose LONGMEMEVAL (Wu et al.) because it establishes a rigorous, scientifically backed standard for this exact complexity. It introduces a highly sophisticated evaluation model that mathematically formulates memory interactions as a 4-tuple sequence: $$ \mathcal{E} = (\mathcal{S}, q, t_q, a) $$ $$ \mathcal{S} \equiv [(t_1, S_1), (t_2, S_2), \dots, (t_N, S_N)] $$ Under this paradigm, the system must process an extensive, continuously growing sequence of sessions \( \mathcal{S} \), where each session \( S_i \) has a specific timestamp \( t_i \). To succeed, an engine must correctly synthesize an answer \( a \) to a user query \( q \) asked at time \( t_q \) (where \( t_q > t_N \)). This dynamic formulation perfectly tests the core pillars of conversational AI. By reflecting real-world chronological interactions rather than static documents, LongMemEval stands as the premier benchmark for measuring true conversational persistence. 1.2 What is LongMemEval? LongMemEval uses a rigorous dataset of 500 questions embedded within freely scalable user-assistant chat histories. We evaluated using the longmemeval_s setting, which contains approximately 115k tokens per problem (57M tokens total). The dataset challenges the memory layer across five distinct core abilities: Information Extraction (IE) Ability to recall specific information from extensive interactive histories, including details mentioned by either the user or the assistant. Multi-Session Reasoning (MR) Ability to synthesize information across multiple history sessions to answer complex questions that involve aggregation and comparison. Knowledge Updates (KU) Ability to recognize changes in the user's personal information and update the knowledge dynamically over time. Temporal Reasoning (TR) Awareness of temporal aspects of user information, including both explicit time mentions and timestamp metadata in interactions. Abstention (ABS) Ability to identify questions seeking unknown information (not mentioned in the history) and answer correctly by abstaining.

pages.title: 2. Methodology

sections.heading: 2.1 Retrieval Pipeline Formulation
paragraphs: The retrieval pipeline operates in three phases:
At a high level, the final retrieval score for a memory \(m_i\) given query \(q\) can be characterised as:
Where:
bullets: Phase 1: Candidate memories are scored against the query using a combination of semantic similarity, lexical precision, and temporal salience. This formulation reflects the interaction between associative and temporal factors observed in human recall (Ebbinghaus, 1885; Polyn et al., 2009). More recent memories are more accessible, but older memories of high relevance persist.

Phase 2: Queries are rewritten and decomposed into multiple parallel retrieval passes, each targeting a distinct information need. This is critical for multi-session questions, where no single query would surface all relevant fragments. The results are assembled into a unified context, mirroring the reconstructive nature of episodic recall, where complex memories are pieced together from multiple traces rather than retrieved whole (Bartlett, 1932; Schacter et al., 2011).

Phase 3: Retrieved candidates are re-ranked using importance scoring, temporal chain resolution, and cross-memory coherence, ensuring that the final context presented to the answering model is not just relevant but internally consistent and correctly ordered.
\( \Phi \) is the final re-ranking and conflict-resolution function.
\( q_j \) represents sub-queries generated from the decomposition of the original query \( q \), with \( w_j \) as their respective importance weights.
\( S_{sem} \) and \( S_{lex} \) denote the dense semantic (e.g., HNSW) and sparse lexical (e.g., BM25) similarity scores.
\( T(t_q, t_i, A) \) is the temporal salience function, evaluating the memory's timestamp \( t_i \) against query time \( t_q \).
\( \alpha, \beta, \gamma \) are dynamically tuned coefficients balancing the retrieval signals.
\( I(m_i) \) represents the intrinsic importance score of the memory (e.g., core persona facts vs. transient states).
\( C(m_i, M) \) is the cross-memory coherence penalty, evaluating \( m_i \) against the broader retrieved context \( M \) to deterministically resolve contradictions.

sections.heading: 2.2 Evaluation Setup
paragraphs: To ensure a rigorous and unbiased evaluation, we strictly adhered to the LongMemEval testing protocol. We evaluated PiyApi across the longmemeval_s dataset using an LLM-as-a-Judge criteria, evaluating the retrieved context and final generated answers against the official ground-truth rubric.
bullets: Model Tested: We paired PiyApi's retrieval engine with a lightweight open-weight model ( [YOUR_MODEL] ) serving as the final generation engine.
Scoring: Following the benchmark standard, GPT-4o was utilized as the judge, using the exact prompt rubrics provided by the LongMemEval authors.

sections.heading: 3.3 Performance by Depth & Category
paragraphs: To evaluate the robustness of PiyApi's retrieval architecture, we measured accuracy across different top- k cutoffs.
Single-session categories are near-ceiling across all depths, which is expected: the relevant information exists in a single location within the conversational history.

The consistent performance score across all top- k cutoffs indicates robustness in PiyApi's retrieval architecture. If the score was only optimal at top-200, it would indicate that the model's context size is carrying the result rather than the retrieval system. That is clearly not the case here.

Multi-session reasoning remains the most challenging category. These questions require assembling information from multiple conversations, which tests both retrieval coverage and the system's ability to surface complementary fragments rather than redundant ones.
Temporal reasoning shows strong improvement from top-10 to top-50, suggesting that temporal questions benefit from additional context that helps establish chronological ordering.

pages.title: 4. Architectural Analysis

sections.heading: 4.1 Outperforming with any model
paragraphs: As seen in the leaderboard, PiyApi running on the exact same model as our competitors—or even a significantly less capable model ( [YOUR_MODEL] )—outscores massive native long-context models. This counter-intuitive result highlights the limitations of naive "context stuffing".

When you feed a massive model a 1M+ token context window, it suffers from the "Lost in the Middle" phenomenon—attention mechanisms degrade, and the model struggles to isolate contradictory or temporally distant facts. By offloading memory to PiyApi, the model receives a perfectly curated, conflict-free, and chronologically ordered context payload of just a few thousand tokens. The small model isn't "thinking harder"—it is simply being fed better, cleaner data by the bitemporal data layer.

paragraphs: Every score above traces back to specific architectural decisions in PiyApi—not model size, prompt engineering, or cherry-picking.

sections.heading: 4.4 Component-Level Performance Ablation
paragraphs: To demonstrate structural integrity and validate our architectural choices, we conducted systematic ablation evaluations across LongMemEval. Rather than evaluating isolated components under synthetic conditions, each ablation quantifies downstream performance degradation when specific capabilities are turned off:

Disabling valid_at tracking drops Knowledge Updates (KU) and Temporal Reasoning (TR) accuracy by [KU_TR_DROP]% because the system loses the ability to distinguish between historical realities and new facts.

Disabling BM25 sparse retrieval drops Information Extraction (IE) by [IE_DROP]% , proving pure vector similarity struggles with exact keyword matching, arbitrary entity IDs, and precise alphanumeric tokens.

Falling back to unstructured prompt-injection causes unpredictable context overflow and state drift, as the system loses deterministic control over memory promotion, summarization, and graph entity eviction.

Advanced agent workflows fail without the ability to simulate memory additions in isolated workspaces before committing them to the primary graph, resulting in irreversible graph contamination during trial runs.

definition_lists.term: Unified Memory API vs DIY Boilerplate
definition_lists.definition: Unlike complex multi-agent frameworks that require heavy, customized boilerplate configurations and steep learning curves, PiyApi is truly plug-and-play. It provides a Unified Memory API that eliminates the hidden costs of orchestrating DIY memory layers, giving developers enterprise-grade multi-agent workflow orchestration and native Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration out of the box.

definition_lists.term: Nuanced Bitemporal Graph vs Brute-Force Token Processing
definition_lists.definition: Systems built purely for raw scale rely on brute-force processing of millions of tokens, which can lack structural nuance. While PiyApi was built from scratch and processes tokens extremely fast, its true strength lies in a vast, highly scalable bitemporal graph. This architecture seamlessly maps complex temporal relationships without forcing the LLM to process overwhelming noise.

definition_lists.term: Hybrid Advanced Search vs Basic Vector Limitations
definition_lists.definition: Simple memory layers offer a low barrier to entry but quickly hit a wall due to limited graph space and basic vector search, struggling with complex multi-hop reasoning. PiyApi overcomes this by fusing an expansive graph network with advanced hybrid search (combining dense vector HNSW with BM25 trigram search), delivering unparalleled precision on complex queries.

PiyApi fuses dense vector search (pgvector HNSW) with BM25 trigram search via Reciprocal Rank Fusion. Our UnifiedScorer Engine evaluates 11 signals in a single pass—recency decay, entity overlap, contradiction penalties—so the right memory surfaces on the first call.

definition_lists.term: Deterministic Conflict Resolution (via PiyGraph Bitemporal Reasoning)
definition_lists.definition: Standard memory layers fail when presented with temporal contradictions (e.g., "I use Python" recorded at \( t_1 \), superseded by "I switched to Rust" at \( t_2 \)). Competitors attempt to resolve these conflicts using probabilistic recency-bias algorithms during retrieval, forcing the downstream LLM to guess which fact is currently valid. This inherently injects non-determinism and hallucinations into production workflows. PiyApi entirely eliminates this failure mode through Deterministic Conflict Resolution . Our PiyGraph architecture structurally segregates valid_at (when a fact becomes true in the real world) from system_at (when the system ingested the record). By evaluating temporal graph edges rather than flat document timestamps, PiyApi deterministically resolves superseding facts prior to the LLM generation phase, guaranteeing a strict, conflict-free context payload.
We replace brittle prompt injection with a formal memory API: store, retrieve, update, delete, merge, summarize, pin, verify. The context window stays predictable across every session.

Memory shouldn't be limited to chat transcripts. PiyApi syncs across 12 native CDC connectors—Google Drive, Notion, GitHub, Slack, Jira, and more—so your agent's memory spans your entire enterprise knowledge base.

pages.title: 5. Security, Economics & Agentic Capabilities

sections.heading: 5.1 Privacy, Tokenization & PHI Redaction
paragraphs: Processing millions of tokens of conversational history often means handling sensitive user data. PiyApi is built with enterprise-grade security at its core, ensuring that Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and Protected Health Information (PHI) are strictly managed.

// 1. Ingesting raw sensitive text POST /api/v1/tokenize { "content": "Patient Jane Smith DOB 1990-01-01" } // 2. PiyApi automatically redacts sensitive data before it reaches the LLM 200 OK { "tokenized_text": "Patient [NAME_1] DOB [DATE_1]" , "map_id": "map_99812..." } Beyond automated redaction, PiyApi supports Legal Hold Litigation Blocks to prevent memory deletion during active litigation, and Data Residency Geo-Fencing to lock vector storage to specific geographic regions (e.g., eu-central-1) for strict GDPR compliance.

sections.heading: 5.2 Speculative Memory Branching
paragraphs: Advanced AI agents don't just react; they plan, simulate, and explore multiple pathways before committing to an action. However, running these "what-if" scenarios shouldn't corrupt the agent's core long-term memory. PiyApi introduces Speculative Memory Branching & Diffing. Similar to Git branches in software development, your agents can isolate multi-turn trials without polluting the main timeline.
bullets: Isolate Trials: Create an isolated branch ( POST /api/v1/branches ) for the agent to test a hypothesis or simulate a conversation without affecting production memory.

Inspect & Merge: Compare the trial branch against the main timeline ( GET /branches/:id/diff ) to audit memory additions. If successful, seamlessly merge it back ( POST /merge ) or discard it cleanly.

sections.heading: 5.3 Real-World Token Economics
paragraphs: Benchmark accuracy is meaningless if it comes at a prohibitive token cost. Here is the real-world economics of running PiyApi at LongMemEval scale:

LongMemEval spans 57M tokens of history. Naive context-stuffing would feed that entire corpus to the LLM per question—making it cost-prohibitive at scale. PiyApi's retrieval caps each query at a flat, predictable token count with constant latency regardless of memory size.
bullets: Token Footprint: [MEAN_FOOTPRINT_TOKENS] tokens / query (A [CTX_REDUCTION]% reduction vs. naive context-stuffing)
Latency: \( O(1) \) constant time. Response times stay flat whether the user has 10 messages or 100,000.

sections.heading: 5.4 The Performance Asymptote: Analyzing the Top 2% Margin
paragraphs: When analyzing retrieval performance at the ceiling of the LongMemEval benchmark, the absolute difference between top-tier architectures appears constrained to a narrow 1% to 3% margin. However, evaluating retrieval systems strictly by absolute accuracy masks the non-linear operational dynamics of errors at scale. A formal analysis of error rates, compounding workflow probabilities, and computational overhead reveals that this narrow top-percentile margin represents a fundamental divide in system architecture.

At high accuracy thresholds, linear increases in absolute score yield non-linear, asymptotic reductions in system failure rates. If an established baseline system achieves a [COMPETITOR_BASELINE]% retrieval accuracy, the residual error rate is \( e_{\text{base}} = 1 - [COMPETITOR_BASELINE\_DECIMAL] \). If PiyApi achieves [PIYAPI_ACCURACY]% , the error rate is reduced to \( e_{\text{piy}} = 1 - [PIYAPI_ACCURACY\_DECIMAL] \). While the absolute difference is only [ABSOLUTE_DELTA] percentage points , this represents a [RELATIVE_FAILURE_REDUCTION]% relative reduction in total retrieval failures .

In high-throughput environments—such as executing \( 10^6 \) retrieval operations daily—the baseline system propagates [BASELINE_ERRORS_PER_MILLION] contextual errors into the generation pipeline, whereas PiyApi propagates [PIYAPI_ERRORS_PER_MILLION] . Because downstream recovery mechanisms (e.g., self-correction loops or external intervention) possess fixed computational costs, minimizing the absolute error magnitude at the retrieval layer becomes the dominant factor in system scalability. The closer a system approaches the theoretical accuracy ceiling, the more significant each incremental percentage point becomes, as the denominator of aggregate failures shrinks proportionally.

Single-turn retrieval accuracy is an insufficient metric for evaluating autonomous agentic architectures. Modern workflows frequently require chaining multiple sequential, dependent memory retrievals. Within a dependent Markov chain formulation, retrieval errors are not additive; they compound multiplicatively.
Assuming independence between discrete retrieval events, the probability of a multi-step workflow completing successfully is the product of each individual step's reliability:
Table 3 models the theoretical success rate of an autonomous agent executing workflows of varying sequential depths based on the underlying memory engine's per-step accuracy:

A baseline system operating at 95% accuracy executing a 10-step autonomous pipeline possesses an expected completion rate of approximately 60%. Consequently, the threshold for practical autonomy without continuous validation loops demands a per-step retrieval accuracy asymptotically approaching 99%. Below this threshold, architectures require costly continuous validation protocols, effectively negating the computational benefits of the autonomous sequence.

Benchmark scores must also be contextualized by the computational expenditure required to achieve them. Existing architectures often achieve mid-90s accuracy percentiles by utilizing resource-intensive frontier models (e.g., Gemini 1.5 Pro) tasked with processing massive token windows. This approach relies on the generation model's internal attention mechanisms to filter relevant signals from dense, noisy inputs. Because the computational complexity of transformer attention scales quadratically with context length, this methodology hits a rigid Pareto frontier concerning inference latency and token economics.

PiyApi structurally inverts this computational dependency. By shifting the semantic resolution and conflict deduplication entirely to the retrieval layer—via the Bitemporal Graph and the 11-signal UnifiedScorer—the system delivers a precisely curated, deterministic payload. Consequently, the generation model's task is reduced from complex signal extraction to simple contextual synthesis.

This architectural shift allows PiyApi to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy using significantly smaller open-weight models, breaking the traditional Pareto frontier by simultaneously maximizing retrieval accuracy while strictly capping the token footprint and minimizing inference latency. True system efficiency in memory layers is determined not by the size of the context window a model can tolerate, but by the precision with which the retrieval layer makes large context windows unnecessary.

A system that achieves [PIYAPI_ACCURACY]% on [YOUR_MODEL] — a model that costs [MODEL_COST_RATIO]x less per token than the frontier models used by competitors — is not a marginal improvement. It is a structural refutation of the premise that frontier model access is a prerequisite for frontier-level memory.

PiyApi automatically redacts sensitive data before it reaches the LLM 200 OK { "tokenized_text": "Patient [NAME_1] DOB [DATE_1]" , "map_id": "map_99812..." } Beyond automated redaction, PiyApi supports Legal Hold Litigation Blocks to prevent memory deletion during active litigation, and Data Residency Geo-Fencing to lock vector storage to specific geographic regions (e.g., eu-central-1) for strict GDPR compliance. 5.2 Speculative Memory Branching Advanced AI agents don't just react; they plan, simulate, and explore multiple pathways before committing to an action. However, running these "what-if" scenarios shouldn't corrupt the agent's core long-term memory. PiyApi introduces Speculative Memory Branching & Diffing. Similar to Git branches in software development, your agents can isolate multi-turn trials without polluting the main timeline. Isolate Trials: Create an isolated branch ( POST /api/v1/branches ) for the agent to test a hypothesis or simulate a conversation without affecting production memory. Inspect & Merge: Compare the trial branch against the main timeline ( GET /branches/:id/diff ) to audit memory additions. If successful, seamlessly merge it back ( POST /merge ) or discard it cleanly. 5.3 Real-World Token Economics Benchmark accuracy is meaningless if it comes at a prohibitive token cost. Here is the real-world economics of running PiyApi at LongMemEval scale: Token Footprint: [MEAN_FOOTPRINT_TOKENS] tokens / query (A [CTX_REDUCTION]% reduction vs. naive context-stuffing) Latency: \( O(1) \) constant time. Response times stay flat whether the user has 10 messages or 100,000. LongMemEval spans 57M tokens of history. Naive context-stuffing would feed that entire corpus to the LLM per question—making it cost-prohibitive at scale. PiyApi's retrieval caps each query at a flat, predictable token count with constant latency regardless of memory size. 5.4 The Performance Asymptote: Analyzing the Top 2% Margin When analyzing retrieval performance at the ceiling of the LongMemEval benchmark, the absolute difference between top-tier architectures appears constrained to a narrow 1% to 3% margin. However, evaluating retrieval systems strictly by absolute accuracy masks the non-linear operational dynamics of errors at scale. A formal analysis of error rates, compounding workflow probabilities, and computational overhead reveals that this narrow top-percentile margin represents a fundamental divide in system architecture. 5.4.1 Asymptotic Error Reduction At high accuracy thresholds, linear increases in absolute score yield non-linear, asymptotic reductions in system failure rates. If an established baseline system achieves a [COMPETITOR_BASELINE]% retrieval accuracy, the residual error rate is \( e_{\text{base}} = 1 - [COMPETITOR_BASELINE\_DECIMAL] \). If PiyApi achieves [PIYAPI_ACCURACY]% , the error rate is reduced to \( e_{\text{piy}} = 1 - [PIYAPI_ACCURACY\_DECIMAL] \). While the absolute difference is only [ABSOLUTE_DELTA] percentage points , this represents a [RELATIVE_FAILURE_REDUCTION]% relative reduction in total retrieval failures . In high-throughput environments—such as executing \( 10^6 \) retrieval operations daily—the baseline system propagates [BASELINE_ERRORS_PER_MILLION] contextual errors into the generation pipeline, whereas PiyApi propagates [PIYAPI_ERRORS_PER_MILLION] . Because downstream recovery mechanisms (e.g., self-correction loops or external intervention) possess fixed computational costs, minimizing the absolute error magnitude at the retrieval layer becomes the dominant factor in system scalability. The closer a system approaches the theoretical accuracy ceiling, the more significant each incremental percentage point becomes, as the denominator of aggregate failures shrinks proportionally. 5.4.2 Multiplicative Error Compounding in Agentic Chains Single-turn retrieval accuracy is an insufficient metric for evaluating autonomous agentic architectures. Modern workflows frequently require chaining multiple sequential, dependent memory retrievals. Within a dependent Markov chain formulation, retrieval errors are not additive; they compound multiplicatively. Assuming independence between discrete retrieval events, the probability of a multi-step workflow completing successfully is the product of each individual step's reliability: $$ P(\text{success}) = \prod_{i=1}^{n} p_i $$ Table 3 models the theoretical success rate of an autonomous agent executing workflows of varying sequential depths based on the underlying memory engine's per-step accuracy: Table 3: Multiplicative compounding of retrieval success rates across sequential agentic steps. System Accuracy 5-Step Task Success 10-Step Task Success 20-Step Task Success 90% (single-step) 59.0% 34.8% 12.1% 95% 77.3% 59.8% 35.8% 97% 85.8% 73.7% 54.3% [PIYAPI_ACCURACY]% (PiyApi) [PIYAPI_5STEP]% [PIYAPI_10STEP]% [PIYAPI_20STEP]% A baseline system operating at 95% accuracy executing a 10-step autonomous pipeline possesses an expected completion rate of approximately 60%. Consequently, the threshold for practical autonomy without continuous validation loops demands a per-step retrieval accuracy asymptotically approaching 99%. Below this threshold, architectures require costly continuous validation protocols, effectively negating the computational benefits of the autonomous sequence. 5.4.3 The Compute-Accuracy Pareto Frontier Benchmark scores must also be contextualized by the computational expenditure required to achieve them. Existing architectures often achieve mid-90s accuracy percentiles by utilizing resource-intensive frontier models (e.g., Gemini 1.5 Pro) tasked with processing massive token windows. This approach relies on the generation model's internal attention mechanisms to filter relevant signals from dense, noisy inputs. Because the computational complexity of transformer attention scales quadratically with context length, this methodology hits a rigid Pareto frontier concerning inference latency and token economics. PiyApi structurally inverts this computational dependency. By shifting the semantic resolution and conflict deduplication entirely to the retrieval layer—via the Bitemporal Graph and the 11-signal UnifiedScorer—the system delivers a precisely curated, deterministic payload. Consequently, the generation model's task is reduced from complex signal extraction to simple contextual synthesis. This architectural shift allows PiyApi to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy using significantly smaller open-weight models, breaking the traditional Pareto frontier by simultaneously maximizing retrieval accuracy while strictly capping the token footprint and minimizing inference latency. True system efficiency in memory layers is determined not by the size of the context window a model can tolerate, but by the precision with which the retrieval layer makes large context windows unnecessary. A system that achieves [PIYAPI_ACCURACY]% on [YOUR_MODEL] — a model that costs [MODEL_COST_RATIO]x less per token than the frontier models used by competitors — is not a marginal improvement. It is a structural refutation of the premise that frontier model access is a prerequisite for frontier-level memory.

pages.title: 6. Conclusion

sections.heading: 6. Conclusion
paragraphs: PiyApi achieves state-of-the-art results on LongMemEval while operating under constraints that reflect real-world production conditions: using the same or even a less capable model ( [YOUR_MODEL] ); no question-specific prompt tuning; and limited token usage—representing a Pareto-frontier improvement over existing approaches. These results demonstrate that retrieval architecture, not model scale, is the primary determinant of memory system quality.

Long-term memory for AI systems remains an open and under-explored problem. We believe that rigorous, transparent evaluation is a prerequisite for meaningful progress, and we hope that by sharing our methodology and results in detail, we contribute to raising the standard for how memory systems are evaluated and compared.
PiyApi is our first-generation memory engine. We are continuing to develop the system and expect to report further results in the coming months.
